0022| 1. Product Overview
0023| The QA Playground Bank Demo is a browser-based simulated banking product intended to model core
0024| digital-banking interactions in a controlled environment. The product provides an authentication boundary, a
0025| banking dashboard, account-oriented functionality and transaction management. QA Playground positions the
0026| Bank Demo as a realistic multi-page banking workflow suitable for end-to-end practice.
0027| �cite�turn0search0�turn0search3�
0028| The application should be understood as a stateful product. Authentication determines access. User/account
0029| state determines what balances and transactions are visible. Financial operations alter application state, and
0030| subsequent views must reflect those committed changes consistently.
0031| 1.1 Product Objectives
0032| •
0033| Provide a realistic but simulated banking environment.
0034| •
0035| Represent multiple user personas with different account/application states.
0036| •
0037| Allow authenticated users to interact with banking entities and financial state.
0038| •
0039| Make account balances and transaction state observable through the user interface.
0040| •
0041| Provide validation and failure states that resemble real application behavior.
0042| •
0043| Provide distinct standard and administrative experiences where supported by the assigned user role.
0044| •
0045| Make the product deterministic enough for repeated functional evaluation while preserving meaningful
0046| stateful behavior.
0047| 1.2 Product Boundaries
0048| •
0049| The product is a simulated banking environment and must not be interpreted as a real banking institution.
0050| •
0051| The credentials listed in this document are demo credentials intentionally exposed by the product.
0052| •
0053| No real monetary value is associated with balances displayed by the application.
0054| •
0055| The product specification covers behavior visible through the application and does not require
0056| implementation-specific APIs or database access.
0057| 2. User Personas and Demo Credentials
0058| The login page explicitly exposes a Test credentials table containing multiple predefined users. These are
0059| product-provided personas/test fixtures and are part of the application's documented behavior.
0060| Username Password Description / Persona State
0061| standard_user bank_sauce Full access
0062| locked_user bank_sauce Locked account
0063| frozen_user bank_sauce Frozen — no transfers
0064| overdraft_user bank_sauce Negative balance
0065| slow_user bank_sauce Slow loading
0066| error_user bank_sauce Wrong loan total
0067| admin_user admin_sauce Admin view
0068| Credential source: These values are transcribed from the Test credentials section visibly presented on the Bank
0069| Demo login page. The page labels the columns Username, Password and Description. The credentials should
0070| therefore be treated as first-class product test data rather than as external assumptions.
0071| 2.1 Persona Requirements
0072| Persona Product requirement
0073| standard_user Must represent the normal/full-access banking experience available to a standard user.
0074| [page 3]
0075| QA Playground — Bank Demo Product PRD Page 3
0076| Persona Product requirement
0077| locked_user Must represent an account in a locked state. The application must enforce the consequences of the locked
0078| state at authentication/access time.
0079| frozen_user Must represent a frozen banking state in which transfers are not permitted, as indicated by the credential
0080| description.
0081| overdraft_user Must represent a user/account state containing a negative balance. The negative balance must remain
0082| internally consistent with the account and transaction state displayed by the application.
0083| slow_user Must exercise the product's intentionally slow-loading behavior. Loading states should remain understandable
0084| and should eventually resolve according to the application's intended behavior.
0085| error_user Must represent the intentionally incorrect loan-total state described by the credential fixture. The application
0086| should expose the corresponding data/error condition consistently wherever that state is represented.
0087| admin_user Must represent the administrative view and expose the administrative capabilities/data intended by the
0088| product.
0089| The descriptions above document the explicit semantics shown on the login page. Where the live application
0090| exposes additional UI, permissions or state-specific behavior for a persona, that behavior is part of the product's
0091| role/state contract and should be consistent throughout the application.
0092| 3. Authentication
0093| 3.1 Login Page
0094| ID Requirement Expected product behavior
0095| AUTH-01 Login entry point The application provides a dedicated login page at the Bank Demo login URL.
0096| AUTH-02 Username input The login interface provides a username field with a clear input affordance.
0097| AUTH-03 Password input The login interface provides a password field and treats entered password content as
0098| obscured input by default.
0099| AUTH-04 Password visibility The visible eye control provides a way to reveal/hide the entered password without
0100| changing the credential.
0101| AUTH-05 Remember me The login interface provides a Remember me checkbox representing an optional
0102| persistence/session preference.
0103| AUTH-06 Sign In A clearly labeled Sign In control submits the authentication request.
0104| AUTH-07 Forgot password A Forgot password entry point is available from the login page.
0105| AUTH-08 Credential fixtures The page visibly provides all seven demo credential records documented in Section 2.
0106| AUTH-09 Valid authentication A valid active credential establishes an authenticated session and exposes the
0107| appropriate post-login experience.
0108| AUTH-10 Invalid authentication Invalid credentials do not grant access and produce an understandable failure state.
0109| AUTH-11 Locked authentication A locked account must not be treated as a normal active session.
0110| 3.2 Session Management
0111| •
0112| An authenticated session must have a clear distinction from the unauthenticated login state.
0113| •
0114| The application must preserve the appropriate user identity while the session is active.
0115| •
0116| Logout must terminate the active authenticated session.
0117| •
0118| After logout, protected banking content must not remain actionable as an authenticated experience.
0119| •
0120| Session persistence behavior must respect the Remember me control when the feature is implemented.
0121| •
0122| Expired or invalid sessions must be handled gracefully rather than leaving the user in a partially authenticated
0123| state.
0124| 4. Dashboard / Home Banking Experience
0125| The dashboard is the authenticated banking overview. It should present the user's relevant banking state and
0126| provide access to the application's supported account and transaction capabilities. QA Playground explicitly
0127| [page 4]
0128| QA Playground — Bank Demo Product PRD Page 4
0129| describes the Bank Demo as including a dashboard. �cite�turn0search0�turn0search1�
0130| ID Requirement Expected product behavior
0131| DASH-01 Authenticated landing A successful active-user login leads to the appropriate authenticated banking experience.
0132| DASH-02 User context The dashboard reflects the authenticated user's persona and associated state.
0133| DASH-03 Account visibility Relevant accounts and balances are represented in the dashboard or reachable through
0134| the banking navigation.
0135| DASH-04 Transaction visibility Relevant transaction/activity information is represented or accessible where supported.
0136| DASH-05 State consistency Dashboard values must remain consistent with the underlying account/transaction state
0137| shown elsewhere in the application.
0138| DASH-06 Role awareness Administrative users receive the intended administrative view rather than being treated
0139| identically to a standard user.
0140| DASH-07 Exceptional states Locked, frozen, overdraft, slow-loading and error-oriented personas must produce their
0141| intended state-specific experience.
0142| 5. Account Management
0143| Account management is a core product domain. The product should allow the authenticated user to interact with
0144| supported banking accounts and maintain accurate account-level state.
0145| ID Requirement Expected product behavior
0146| ACCT-01 Account listing The user can view the accounts available to the current user.
0147| ACCT-02 Account identity Each account is distinguishable by its displayed name/identifier and any supported
0148| account type information.
0149| ACCT-03 Account balance Each account exposes a current balance consistent with committed financial operations.
0150| ACCT-04 Account creation Where the live product provides account creation, an authenticated user can provide the
0151| required account information and create an account.
0152| ACCT-05 Account validation Required account fields are validated before an invalid account can be committed.
0153| ACCT-06 Account persistence A successfully created account remains available according to the application's
0154| persistence model.
0155| ACCT-07 Account state Special states such as frozen or overdraft must be reflected accurately in account
0156| behavior and displayed state.
0157| ACCT-08 Account consistency The same account must not display contradictory balances or identity information across
0158| product surfaces.
0159| 5.1 Account Data Model
0160| Data element Purpose
0161| Account identifier/name Human-readable identification of the banking account.
0162| Account type Classification of the account where supported by the product.
0163| Current balance Current monetary state of the account.
0164| Account status Active, frozen, locked or other state where exposed.
0165| Associated user User/persona to whom the account belongs.
0166| Transaction history Financial events associated with the account where supported.
0167| 6. Transaction Management
0168| Transaction management covers financial events that change or represent account state. The public product
0169| description explicitly identifies transaction management as a core Bank Demo capability.
0170| �cite�turn0search0�turn0search2�
0171| ID Requirement Expected product behavior
0172| TXN-01 Transaction visibility Users can view supported transaction/activity information associated with their banking
0173| state.
0174| [page 5]
0175| QA Playground — Bank Demo Product PRD Page 5
0176| ID Requirement Expected product behavior
0177| TXN-02 Transaction amount A transaction displays the amount associated with the financial event.
0178| TXN-03 Transaction direction Where relevant, the UI distinguishes money entering versus leaving an account.
0179| TXN-04 Transaction account A transaction can be associated with the relevant account(s).
0180| TXN-05 Transaction state Only committed financial changes should be represented as completed financial state.
0181| TXN-06 Balance relationship Completed transactions must reconcile with the displayed account balances.
0182| TXN-07 History persistence Committed transaction history should remain available according to the application's
0183| persistence model.
0184| TXN-08 Failure handling Rejected operations must not create misleading completed transaction records.
0185| 7. Money Movement / Transfers
0186| Transfers are part of the banking product's state-changing behavior. The documented frozen-user credential
0187| explicitly states 'no transfers', establishing that transfer permission is persona/state dependent.
0188| ID Requirement Expected product behavior
0189| TRF-01 Transfer capability The product provides a supported transfer mechanism where permitted for the current
0190| user/account state.
0191| TRF-02 Source selection A transfer identifies the account from which funds are moved.
0192| TRF-03 Destination selection A transfer identifies the account receiving funds.
0193| TRF-04 Amount A transfer contains a monetary amount subject to product validation.
0194| TRF-05 Positive amount Invalid monetary values must not be silently accepted as successful transfers.
0195| TRF-06 Sufficient funds The product must apply its supported balance/overdraft rules when determining whether
0196| a transfer can complete.
0197| TRF-07 Frozen restriction The frozen persona must not be permitted to perform transfers, consistent with its explicit
0198| fixture description.
0199| TRF-08 Atomicity A failed transfer must not leave the source and destination in an inconsistent
0200| partially-updated state.
0201| TRF-09 Balance update A completed transfer must produce consistent source and destination balance changes.
0202| TRF-10 Transaction record A completed transfer must be represented in transaction/activity history where that
0203| feature is exposed.
0204| 8. Deposits / Funding / Balance Changes
0205| Where the live Bank Demo exposes deposit, add-funds or equivalent balance-increase functionality, it forms part
0206| of the account state-management domain.
0207| ID Requirement Expected product behavior
0208| FUND-01 Funding action Supported users can initiate the product's supported balance-increase operation.
0209| FUND-02 Amount validation The monetary input must obey the application's accepted numeric and business rules.
0210| FUND-03 Balance update A successful funding operation increases the appropriate balance by the committed
0211| amount.
0212| FUND-04 Transaction linkage A successful funding operation is reflected in transaction history where supported.
0213| FUND-05 Failure integrity A failed funding operation must not create a false balance or completed transaction.
0214| 9. Overdraft State
0215| The overdraft_user fixture explicitly represents a negative-balance condition. This makes overdraft handling an
0216| intentional product state rather than an accidental edge case.
0217| •
0218| The application must be capable of displaying a negative balance for the overdraft persona.
0219| •
0220| The negative balance must be displayed consistently wherever the account balance appears.
0221| [page 6]
0222| QA Playground — Bank Demo Product PRD Page 6
0223| •
0224| Transaction/activity information must reconcile with the negative balance.
0225| •
0226| Any transfer/funding rules involving an overdraft state must follow the application's defined business rules
0227| rather than assuming that all negative balances are invalid.
0228| •
0229| The overdraft state must not be visually or semantically confused with an application error.
0230| 10. Special Persona States
0231| 10.1 Locked User
0232| •
0233| The locked_user fixture represents an explicitly locked account.
0234| •
0235| Authentication must respect the locked state.
0236| •
0237| The application must provide a clear user-visible outcome when a locked account attempts to authenticate.
0238| •
0239| A locked state must not accidentally grant the same access as standard_user.
0240| 10.2 Frozen User
0241| •
0242| The frozen_user fixture represents a frozen account with the explicit restriction 'no transfers'.
0243| •
0244| The user may still be able to authenticate/view permitted information depending on the product's
0245| implementation.
0246| •
0247| Transfer functionality must be unavailable, disabled or rejected for this persona.
0248| •
0249| The restriction must not be bypassable through normal UI interaction.
0250| 10.3 Slow User
0251| •
0252| The slow_user fixture represents intentionally slow-loading behavior.
0253| •
0254| The application should communicate loading/progress rather than appearing permanently broken.
0255| •
0256| Once loading completes, the resulting state should be internally consistent.
0257| •
0258| Slow behavior should not cause duplicate submissions or contradictory state when the user waits for
0259| completion.
0260| 10.4 Error User
0261| •
0262| The error_user fixture is explicitly described as 'Wrong loan total'.
0263| •
0264| The product must expose the intended incorrect-loan-total condition in the relevant
0265| administrative/dashboard/loan-related representation if present.
0266| •
0267| The error state should remain distinguishable from network failure or generic application failure.
0268| •
0269| Other unrelated banking values should not become corrupted merely because this persona contains the
0270| intentional loan-total discrepancy.
0271| 10.5 Admin User
0272| •
0273| The admin_user fixture represents the administrative view.
0274| •
0275| Administrative authentication must lead to the intended administrative experience.
0276| •
0277| Administrative information and controls should be distinguishable from ordinary customer-facing banking
0278| information.
0279| •
0280| Administrative capabilities must be restricted to the administrative persona where the product defines
0281| role-based access.
0282| •
0283| A standard user must not automatically inherit administrative-only capabilities.
0284| 11. Loan / Loan-Total Representation
0285| [page 7]
0286| QA Playground — Bank Demo Product PRD Page 7
0287| The existence of the error_user fixture with the description 'Wrong loan total' establishes that the product
0288| includes, or is intended to include, a loan-related total or representation in at least one banking view.
0289| ID Requirement Expected product behavior
0290| LOAN-01 Loan information Where the product exposes loan information, it should identify the relevant loan/account
0291| context.
0292| LOAN-02 Loan total The product should display a loan total according to the current user's state.
0293| LOAN-03 Error fixture error_user must expose the intentionally incorrect loan-total state described by its
0294| credential fixture.
0295| LOAN-04 Consistency Loan totals should be internally consistent with any supporting loan data displayed in the
0296| same view.
0297| LOAN-05 Error isolation An intentional loan-total discrepancy must not incorrectly alter unrelated account
0298| balances or transactions.
0299| 12. Validation and Error Handling
0300| The Bank Demo is explicitly positioned as a practice application involving forms and validations.
0301| �cite�turn0search2�
0302| Domain Validation expectation
0303| Username Required for authentication; malformed or unknown values must not authenticate.
0304| Password Required for authentication; incorrect values must not authenticate.
0305| Account fields Required account information must be validated before creation/commit.
0306| Monetary inputs Must accept only values supported by the application's business rules and formatting rules.
0307| Transfer source/destination Must identify valid eligible accounts.
0308| Transfer amount Must comply with numeric, positivity and available-funds/business-rule constraints.
0309| Permission restrictions Actions unavailable to a persona must be blocked or clearly rejected.
0310| Network/loading failures The user should receive an understandable state instead of silent data loss.
0311| State conflicts The product must avoid partial updates when a state-changing operation fails.
0312| 13. Data Integrity and Consistency
0313| •
0314| An account's displayed balance must represent its committed financial state.
0315| •
0316| Transaction records and balances must agree after successful financial operations.
0317| •
0318| A rejected transaction must not appear as completed financial activity.
0319| •
0320| A user must not see another user's private account information through normal navigation.
0321| •
0322| Role-specific data must remain consistent with the authenticated persona.
0323| •
0324| The same account must retain a stable identity across dashboard, account and transaction views.
0325| •
0326| State-changing operations should be idempotent from the user's perspective with respect to duplicate
0327| submissions where the product can detect them.
0328| •
0329| Refreshing or navigating between supported banking views should not arbitrarily revert committed data.
0330| 14. Authorization and Access Control
0331| Area Requirement
0332| Unauthenticated state Protected banking information and operations must not be available as an authenticated experience.
0333| Standard user Receives the normal/full-access experience represented by standard_user.
0334| Locked user Receives the restricted behavior associated with a locked account.
0335| Frozen user Cannot perform transfers, consistent with the fixture description.
0336| [page 8]
0337| QA Playground — Bank Demo Product PRD Page 8
0338| Area Requirement
0339| Admin user Receives the administrative view and associated authorized capabilities.
0340| Cross-user isolation A user should not be able to access another user's account information merely by manipulating normal
0341| UI navigation.
0342| Session identity All user-specific dashboard/account/transaction data must correspond to the currently authenticated
0343| identity.
0344| 15. User Interface and Experience Requirements
0345| Area Requirement
0346| Login Username/password fields, password visibility control, Remember me, Sign In and Forgot password are
0347| clearly presented.
0348| Credential reference The Test credentials section clearly presents username, password and description for all predefined
0349| personas.
0350| Navigation Authenticated users can discover the product's supported banking areas through visible navigation.
0351| Feedback Successful and failed state-changing operations have clear user-visible feedback.
0352| Loading Slow or asynchronous operations communicate that work is in progress.
0353| Errors Errors are understandable, associated with the relevant operation and do not silently discard user input
0354| when recovery is possible.
0355| Balances Monetary values are displayed consistently and unambiguously.
0356| Tables/lists Account and transaction collections should clearly associate each row/item with its relevant data.
0357| Responsive behavior Core banking controls remain usable at supported viewport sizes.
0358| 16. Accessibility Requirements
0359| •
0360| Form fields should have accessible labels or equivalent accessible names.
0361| •
0362| The password visibility control should expose an understandable accessible name.
0363| •
0364| Checkboxes and actionable controls should be keyboard operable.
0365| •
0366| Validation and error messages should be discoverable by assistive technologies where practical.
0367| •
0368| Color should not be the only mechanism for communicating success, failure, restriction or state.
0369| •
0370| Loading states should be communicated in a way that does not leave assistive-technology users without
0371| feedback.
0372| 17. Security Requirements for the Simulated Product
0373| Although the Bank Demo uses intentionally public demo credentials, it should still model sensible
0374| banking-product security boundaries.
0375| •
0376| Passwords must be handled as password input and not displayed in plaintext by default.
0377| •
0378| Protected banking views should require an appropriate authenticated session.
0379| •
0380| Logout must invalidate the active authenticated experience.
0381| •
0382| Authorization should be enforced consistently across user personas.
0383| •
0384| A frozen/locked restriction must not be bypassable through ordinary UI actions.
0385| •
0386| Administrative views must not be exposed to ordinary users.
0387| •
0388| User-specific financial information must remain scoped to the authenticated identity.
0389| •
0390| Error messages should avoid exposing unnecessary implementation details.

0406| 19. Product State Model
0407| State Meaning Product expectation
0408| Unauthenticated No active user session Only public/login functionality is available.
0409| Authenticated Valid user session User-specific banking information and permitted operations are
0410| available.
0411| Locked Account is locked Normal active-user access is restricted.
0412| Frozen Account is frozen Transfer capability is prohibited.
0413| Overdraft Account has negative balance Negative balance is represented as a valid special account state.
0414| Loading Application is retrieving/processing data Progress is communicated and final state resolves consistently.
0415| Error Intentionally incorrect or failed
0416| application state
0417| Error condition is visible without corrupting unrelated data.
0418| Administrative Admin persona/session Administrative view and authorized data are exposed.
0419| Logged out Session terminated Protected banking state is no longer actionable as authenticated
0420| content.

0461| 22. Out-of-Scope Assumptions
0462| •
0463| This PRD does not assume undocumented banking products such as cards, mortgages, investments or bill pay
0464| unless they are visibly present in the live application.
0465| •
0466| This PRD does not prescribe a fixed sequence of user actions.
0467| •
0468| This PRD does not define automation implementation, selectors, APIs or framework-specific behavior.
0469| •
0470| Where a feature is conditionally present in the live UI, its current live behavior is authoritative.
